section: Banking sector reforms - Narasimham Committee I and II, Basel norms, bank mergers, privatisation debate
subsections: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS

accepted.s: The Basel Accords are framed by which of the following bodies?
o: International Organization of Securities Commissions under the BIS
Financial Stability Board under the International Monetary Fund
Basel Committee on Banking Supervision under the Bank for International Settlements
International Monetary Fund under the World Bank
accepted.x: The Basel Accords are formulated by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS), which functions under the Bank for International Settlements (BIS).
accepted.tq: Identify the correct international body and distinguish it from neighbouring financial institutions.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) was established in which year?
accepted.x: The BIS was established in 1930 and is described as the world's oldest international financial organisation.
accepted.tq: Use the year-based elimination method with closely spaced numerical options.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the principal focus of Basel I?
o: Stable funding over a one-year horizon
Liquidity coverage over a 30-day stress period
Market discipline through mandatory public disclosure alone
Credit risk and a minimum capital standard of 8 per cent of risk-weighted assets
accepted.x: Basel I, introduced in 1988, primarily addressed credit risk and prescribed minimum capital of 8 per cent of risk-weighted assets.
accepted.tq: Match the accord with its core content rather than with a later liquidity norm.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Basel I:
1. It was introduced in 1988.
2. It dealt primarily with credit risk.
3. It prescribed five risk-weight categories of 0, 10, 20, 50 and 100 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Basel I was introduced in 1988, focused on credit risk and used five risk-weight categories: 0, 10, 20, 50 and 100 per cent.
accepted.tq: Check each numerical statement separately before selecting the inclusive combination.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following sets correctly represents the three pillars of Basel II?
o: Capital adequacy, monetary stability and deposit insurance
Credit risk, exchange-rate risk and sovereign risk
Liquidity coverage, stable funding and countercyclical lending
Minimum capital requirements, supervisory review and market discipline
accepted.x: Basel II rests on three pillars: minimum capital requirements, supervisory review and market discipline.
accepted.tq: Recall the standard three-part framework and reject terms belonging to Basel III liquidity norms.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following Basel-related developments in chronological order:
A. Basel I
B. Introduction of CRAR in India
C. Basel II
D. Basel III
accepted.x: Basel I was issued in 1988, India introduced CRAR in 1992, Basel II followed in 2004, and Basel III emerged after the 2007–09 financial crisis.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the Indian reform between them.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Basel III was developed principally as a response to which circumstance?
o: The Asian financial crisis of 1997–98 alone
The introduction of the euro in 1999
The sovereign debt crisis of the 1980s
accepted.x: Basel III was formulated after the global financial crisis of 2007–09 to strengthen bank capital, liquidity and resilience.
accepted.tq: Link the reform to its triggering crisis rather than to an unrelated financial event.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Basel III norms were introduced in India from:
accepted.x: India began implementing Basel III norms from 1 January 2013.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Indian implementation date from the global post-crisis origin of Basel III.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a feature associated with Basel III?
o: Five fixed credit-risk buckets of 0, 10, 20, 50 and 100 per cent
Liquidity Coverage Ratio and Net Stable Funding Ratio
accepted.x: The five fixed risk-weight buckets are associated with Basel I. Basel III introduced stronger CET1 requirements, buffers, leverage and liquidity standards.
accepted.tq: Find the item belonging to the earlier accord rather than the modern framework.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Basel III seeks to improve the quality and quantity of bank capital.
2. Basel III introduces capital buffers and a leverage ratio.
3. Basel III includes liquidity standards such as LCR and NSFR.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements describe major elements of Basel III, including better capital, buffers, leverage control and liquidity standards.
accepted.tq: Test whether all statements belong to the same reform package before choosing the comprehensive option.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
In the context of Basel III, the three broad objectives described as its pillars are to:
1. Absorb shocks
2. Improve risk management and governance
3. Improve transparency and disclosure
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The three stated Basel III objectives are absorption of shocks, improvement of risk management and governance, and improvement of transparency and disclosure.
accepted.tq: Treat the three-item objective list as a complete set and check each item for inclusion.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: India introduced the Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) in 1992. Under the Basel I framework, India prescribed CRAR at:
accepted.x: India introduced CRAR in 1992 and prescribed it at 9 per cent under Basel I, one percentage point above the Basel minimum of 8 per cent.
accepted.tq: Separate the Indian norm from the lower international minimum.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly expresses the relationship between the BCBS minimum and the RBI norm for total CRAR?
o: BCBS 8 per cent; RBI 9 per cent
BCBS 9 per cent; RBI 8 per cent
BCBS 4.5 per cent; RBI 5.5 per cent
BCBS 10.5 per cent; RBI 11.5 per cent
accepted.x: The BCBS minimum total CRAR is 8 per cent, whereas the RBI norm is 9 per cent. The figures of 10.5 and 11.5 per cent include the capital conservation buffer.
accepted.tq: Compare the base ratio with the ratio including the buffer before selecting the pair.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Ratio or buffer)
a. Common Equity Tier 1
b. Tier 1 capital
c. Capital conservation buffer
d. Countercyclical capital buffer

List-II (BCBS minimum or range)
i. 0–2.5 per cent
ii. 2.5 per cent
iii. 4.5 per cent
iv. 6 per cent

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: The BCBS minimums are CET1 4.5 per cent, Tier 1 capital 6 per cent, CCB 2.5 per cent and countercyclical buffer 0–2.5 per cent.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive buffer range and then complete the capital-ratio pairs.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes capital conservation buffer from countercyclical capital buffer?
o: The former is fixed at 2.5 per cent and the latter ranges from 0 to 2.5 per cent.
The former is 0–2.5 per cent and the latter is fixed at 2.5 per cent.
Both are fixed at 2.5 per cent under all circumstances.
Both are variable between 2.5 and 5 per cent.
accepted.x: The capital conservation buffer is 2.5 per cent, while the countercyclical capital buffer can range from 0 to 2.5 per cent.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two similarly named buffers by their fixed and variable values.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The principal purpose of the countercyclical capital buffer is to:
o: Guarantee stable funding for one year
Check excessive credit growth during an upswing
Ensure survival during a 30-day liquidity stress
Replace Tier 1 capital with subordinated debt
accepted.x: The countercyclical capital buffer is intended to restrain excessive credit growth and strengthen bank resilience during credit booms.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy instrument from the economic problem it is designed to address.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In India, the countercyclical capital buffer framework was introduced by the RBI in 2015. Its main trigger is the:
accepted.x: The RBI introduced the countercyclical capital buffer framework in 2015, with the credit-to-GDP gap as its main trigger.
accepted.tq: Match the macroeconomic indicator with the regulatory buffer it activates.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement regarding India's countercyclical capital buffer is correct?
o: A framework has existed since 2015, but the buffer has not been activated.
India has no framework for it because it is not part of Basel III.
It has been permanently activated at 2.5 per cent since 2015.
It was replaced by the capital conservation buffer in 2020.
accepted.x: India has had a countercyclical capital buffer framework since 2015, but the buffer has not been activated.
accepted.tq: Watch for the trap that treats the existence of a framework as its activation.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The minimum leverage ratio prescribed by the BCBS is:
accepted.x: The BCBS minimum leverage ratio is 3 per cent. The RBI prescribes 4 per cent for domestic systemically important banks and 3.5 per cent for other banks.
accepted.tq: Separate the international floor from the higher differentiated Indian norms.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the RBI's leverage-ratio norms?
o: 3.5 per cent for D-SIBs and 4 per cent for other banks
3 per cent for D-SIBs and 2.5 per cent for other banks
4 per cent for D-SIBs and 3.5 per cent for other banks
5 per cent for D-SIBs and 4.5 per cent for other banks
accepted.x: The RBI prescribes a leverage ratio of 4 per cent for domestic systemically important banks and 3.5 per cent for other banks.
accepted.tq: Read the differentiated category-wise norm carefully and avoid reversing the two classes.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The leverage ratio was introduced as a Basel requirement under:
accepted.x: The leverage ratio came with Basel III as a non-risk-weighted backstop to prevent balance sheets from expanding on a thin capital base.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the later Basel III safeguard from the earlier capital frameworks.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A bank is required to maintain sufficient high-quality liquid assets to withstand a 30-day stress scenario. Which regulatory measure is being applied?
accepted.x: The Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) requires a stock of high-quality liquid assets sufficient to survive a 30-day stress period.
accepted.tq: Map the time horizon in the scenario to the corresponding liquidity ratio.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: NSFR — survival during a 30-day stress period
LCR — stable funding over one year
LCR — high-quality liquid assets for a 30-day stress period
CCyB — high-quality liquid assets for a 30-day stress period
accepted.x: LCR concerns high-quality liquid assets adequate for a 30-day stress period. NSFR concerns stable funding over a one-year horizon.
accepted.tq: Use the time-period distinction to eliminate swapped definitions.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Net Stable Funding Ratio (NSFR) is concerned primarily with:
o: The credit-to-GDP gap during a boom
Capital adequacy during a 30-day stress period
Credit risk weights over five categories
Stable funding over a one-year horizon
accepted.x: NSFR promotes stable funding over a one-year horizon, whereas LCR addresses short-term liquidity over 30 days.
accepted.tq: Recall the longer liquidity horizon and contrast it with the short-term LCR.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following are classified as Level 1 high-quality liquid assets for the purpose of LCR?
1. Cash
2. Government securities
3. Central-bank reserves
4. Highly rated corporate bonds
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Cash, government securities and central-bank reserves are Level 1 HQLA. Highly rated corporate bonds are classified as Level 2 HQLA.
accepted.tq: Separate the core Level 1 assets from the corporate-bond example belonging to Level 2.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The minimum LCR and NSFR prescribed in the comparative Basel-RBI framework are:
o: LCR 100 per cent and NSFR 100 per cent
LCR 100 per cent and NSFR 90 per cent
LCR 110 per cent and NSFR 110 per cent
LCR 90 per cent and NSFR 100 per cent
accepted.x: The comparative framework lists both the LCR and NSFR minimums at 100 per cent for BCBS and RBI norms.
accepted.tq: Treat paired ratio figures independently and identify the matching value.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The RBI deferred the revised LCR norms up to:
accepted.x: The RBI deferred the revised Liquidity Coverage Ratio norms up to 31 March 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the regulatory deferral date from the general LCR implementation period.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly defines Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR) or CRAR?
o: Total capital divided by risk-weighted assets
Total deposits divided by total advances
Tier 1 capital divided by total non-risk-weighted exposure
Liquid assets divided by short-term liabilities
accepted.x: CAR or CRAR is calculated as capital divided by risk-weighted assets. The leverage ratio, in contrast, uses total non-risk-weighted exposure.
accepted.tq: Distinguish risk-weighted capital adequacy from the non-risk-weighted leverage measure.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the components of regulatory capital is correct?
o: Tier 1 capital is composed exclusively of subordinated debt.
Tier 1 capital includes pure equity elements, while Tier 2 may include subordinated debt.
Tier 2 capital consists only of paid-up equity and reserves.
Both Tier 1 and Tier 2 consist entirely of government securities.
accepted.x: Tier 1 capital includes paid-up capital, reserves and undistributed profits as core equity. Tier 2 has a mixed equity-debt character and may include subordinated debt.
accepted.tq: Use the core-versus-supplementary capital distinction to identify the accurate composition.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly presents the RBI norms for CET1, Tier 1 capital and total CRAR?
accepted.x: The RBI norms listed are CET1 5.5 per cent, Tier 1 capital 7 per cent and total CRAR 9 per cent.
accepted.tq: Read the three-column ratio comparison without substituting the BCBS minimums.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: When the capital conservation buffer is included, the total CRAR requirement becomes:
o: 10.5 per cent under BCBS and 11.5 per cent under RBI
11.5 per cent under BCBS and 12.5 per cent under RBI
8 per cent under BCBS and 9 per cent under RBI
9 per cent under BCBS and 10 per cent under RBI
accepted.x: Adding the 2.5 per cent capital conservation buffer gives 10.5 per cent for the BCBS minimum and 11.5 per cent for the RBI norm.
accepted.tq: Add the buffer to the respective base ratio instead of confusing the two totals.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In October 2025, the RBI proposed lower risk weights under Basel III for which of the following sectors?
accepted.x: In October 2025, the RBI proposed lower Basel III risk weights for MSMEs and real estate.
accepted.tq: Use the sector-pair association while rejecting plausible but unlisted alternatives.
accepted.sec: Basel Accords I, II, III - pillars, capital ratios, leverage ratio, CCB, LCR, NSFR, RBI vs BCBS  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The regulatory CAR norm and the own CAR figure mentioned for HDFC Bank are, respectively:
accepted.x: HDFC Bank's regulatory CAR norm is 11.9 per cent, while its own reported CAR is 19.6 per cent.
accepted.tq: Read the order of the figures carefully: regulatory requirement first and bank's actual figure second.
